title: Judges 2
paragraphs: ¹ The angel of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bokim and said, "I brought you out of Egypt and led you into the land I swore to give your ancestors. I said I would never break my covenant with you, ² but you must make no agreement with the people of this land — you must tear down their altars. Yet you have disobeyed me. Why have you done this? ³ Now I tell you, I will not drive them out before you; they will become thorns in your sides, and their gods will be a trap for you." ⁴ When the angel of the LORD said these things to all the Israelites, the people wept aloud. ⁵ They named that place Bokim and offered sacrifices there to the LORD.

⁶ When Joshua had dismissed the people, the Israelites each went to take possession of their own allotted territory. ⁷ The people served the LORD throughout Joshua's lifetime and throughout the lifetimes of the elders who outlived him — those who had seen all the great things the LORD had done for Israel. ⁸ Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of a hundred and ten. ⁹ He was buried within the borders of his own inheritance at Timnath-heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash. ¹⁰ After that whole generation was gone, a new generation grew up who knew nothing of the LORD or the things he had done for Israel.

¹¹ Then the Israelites did evil in the LORD's sight and served the Baals. ¹² They abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors who had brought them out of Egypt, and they followed other gods — the gods of the surrounding peoples. They bowed down to those gods and provoked the LORD to anger. ¹³ They abandoned the LORD and served Baal and the Ashtoreths. ¹⁴ The LORD's anger burned against Israel, and he handed them over to raiders who plundered them. He sold them to their enemies all around, so that Israel could no longer hold its ground against them. ¹⁵ Whenever Israel went out to fight, the LORD's hand was against them for disaster, just as he had warned and sworn he would do. They were in great distress.

¹⁶ But the LORD raised up judges who rescued Israel from the hands of those who plundered them. ¹⁷ Yet the people would not listen to their judges; they chased after other gods, bowing down to them. They quickly turned from the path their ancestors had walked — the path of obedience to the LORD's commands. ¹⁸ Whenever the LORD raised up a judge for them, he was with that judge and rescued the people from their enemies as long as the judge lived — for the LORD had compassion on them as they groaned under their oppressors. ¹⁹ But when the judge died, the people returned to their corrupt ways, behaving even worse than their ancestors. They would not give up their evil practices or their stubborn ways. ²⁰ So the LORD's anger burned against Israel, and he said, "Because this nation has violated the covenant I commanded their ancestors and has not listened to me,

²¹ I will no longer drive out before them any of the nations Joshua left when he died. ²² Through them I will test Israel — to see whether they will keep the way of the LORD and walk in it as their ancestors did, or not." ²³ That is why the LORD left those nations in place, rather than quickly driving them out. He had not handed them over to Joshua.
